messages:
zoe (People Ops): Raj just emailed asking whether he can roll a 401(k) from his last employer into our plan mid-year and if that affects his HSA/FSA election limits. Anyone have a quick checklist we can send him?

mike (Benefits): Short checklist: 1) Confirm our plan accepts incoming rollovers (we do). 2) Determine rollover type: direct trustee-to-trustee rollover (preferred) vs check payable to employee (risk of withholding). 3) Rollover doesn't change current year elective deferral limits, but after-tax/ROTH in-plan rollovers have special rules.

hana (Payroll): From payroll side: we only need the rollover paperwork for recordkeeping; payroll doesn't process rollovers. But note: if Raj wants to do an in-plan Roth conversion or after-tax rollover, that may have taxable implications and we should coordinate with payroll for withholding if taxable.

raj (IC): Can I roll money from a former 401(k) that has both pre-tax and Roth after-tax portions into our plan? I also increased my HSA deferral at open enrollment and want to make sure I don't exceed limits.

mike (Benefits): You can roll pre-tax to our pre-tax 401(k). Roth 401(k) amounts can often roll to a Roth 401(k) or Roth IRA depending on vendor rules. Some vendors treat after-tax (non-Roth) differently; if it's after-tax non-Roth, you might be able to roll the after-tax portion to an after-tax account or do an in-plan conversion to Roth (taxable). We'll need the source plan's distribution code.

zoe (People Ops): Quick Q for clarity: does doing a rollover change your annual contribution limit? i.e., if I roll in $50k, can I still contribute up to the 2026 deferral limit?

mike (Benefits): Good call  rollovers do NOT count toward the annual deferral limit. You still have the full elective deferral limit (e.g., $23,000 for 2026 hypothetical) to contribute via payroll. Rollover is separate from YTD employee deferrals.

hana (Payroll): Note on HSA: HSA contributions are separate and have their own IRS limits (individual/family). Rolling a 401(k) doesn't affect HSA contribution room. FSA plan year is independent too. If Raj wants to max HSA after rollover, it's fine.

raj (IC): If the former vendor sends a check payable to me (the employee) and there's 20% mandatory withholding, can I avoid that? I want the full amount moved.

mike (Benefits): You can avoid withholding by requesting a direct rollover (check payable to the new plan/trustee). If you receive a check to you, you have 60 days to deposit into an IRA/plan to avoid taxation, but that 20% withholding would still have occurred and you'd need to make up the withheld amount from personal funds to get the full rollover treatment. So direct is best.

benefits-bot: Ticket ROLL-2026-304 created: "Rollover acceptance + documentation needed for Raj". Attachments requested: copy of distribution form, 401k plan summary from prior employer, and participant ID.

zoe (People Ops): Action items: Mike to send template email with steps and docs Raj should request from prior admin. Hana to note any payroll coordination if there's taxable in-plan conversion. I'll reply to Raj with the checklist and link to the ticket.

mike (Benefits): Template snippet below (to send Raj):

```
Hi Raj,
To complete a direct rollover into Redwood 401(k):
1) Ask your previous plan admin for a trustee-to-trustee direct rollover payable to: "Redwood Inference 401(k) Plan, FBO Raj [last name]" and request a distribution code showing pre-tax vs Roth vs after-tax breakdown.
2) Send the rollover paperwork and distribution summary to benefits@redwood.com.
3) If any amount is taxable (e.g., in-plan Roth conversion), we'll coordinate with Payroll for withholding guidance.
4) Rolling funds does NOT affect your 2026 elective deferral limit.

We'll confirm receipt and upload documents to your file.
Thanks,
Mike (Benefits)
```

hana (Payroll): I'll add a payroll note: if there's an in-plan Roth conversion request, notify payroll at least 5 business days before the pay run so we can set up tax withholding; otherwise no payroll action required.

raj (IC): Perfect  please add how to handle loan balances from the old plan? Mine has a small outstanding loan.

mike (Benefits): Loan balances typically cannot be rolled into a new employer plan as a loan. Options: (a) repay loan before rollover, (b) request distribution (could be taxable), or (c) leave the loan with the old plan if allowed. We'll ask the prior admin for options. Add that to ROLL-2026-304.

zoe (People Ops): Thanks team. Raj  I'll send the checklist now and link you to the ticket. If anyone sees issues with Roth mapping or after-tax buckets when paperwork arrives, flag here. :thumbsup:
